source_references.excerpt: A customer places an order. Every order belongs to exactly one customer, and customers can place multiple orders over time. Each customer has a unique customer ID in the CRM system.

ambiguities.description: Customer 'Client' terminology: The billing team uses the term 'client' for customers but with a different definition—only considering someone a client after they've paid. Is 'Client' a subtype of 'Customer' (restricted to those who have paid), or are these two entirely separate entity types? Should the model include a fact type 'Customer makes Payment' with a corresponding constraint that only customers with payments are clients?

source_references.excerpt: I've heard some people call customers 'clients' in the billing system. Are those the same thing? Good question. In our CRM they're 'customers' but the billing team calls them 'clients.' For our purposes they're the same concept but the billing team has a slightly different definition -- they only consider someone a client once they've actually paid.

ambiguities.description: Customer name uniqueness: The model assumes each customer has at most one name, but the transcript does not explicitly confirm this. Could a customer record have multiple names (e.g., display name and legal name) or could a name be updated over time? Is name history tracked?

source_references.excerpt: Yes, every customer has a name. It's just a text field.

ambiguities.description: Temporal state of order-customer relationship: The model captures that 'Customer places Order' is a current-state relationship, but the transcript does not clarify whether orders must remain linked to the original customer if a customer account is merged, deleted, or changed. Should there be temporal tracking of which customer placed an order at a specific point in time?

source_references.excerpt: A customer places an order. Every order belongs to exactly one customer, and customers can place multiple orders over time.

ambiguities.description: Quantity data type and constraints: Quantity is modeled as an integer, but the transcript does not specify whether fractional quantities are allowed (e.g., 2.5 units) or a minimum positive quantity. Should quantity have a positive constraint (> 0)?

ambiguities.description: Order line granularity: An order line is implicitly represented as the ternary relationship 'Order contains Product with Quantity', but it is never explicitly named or treated as an entity in its own right. Should an 'OrderLine' entity be created with its own identifier to support additional attributes (e.g., line-level discount, shipment status per line)?
